**The document does not report an average treatment effect or p-value for a short-term homepage engagement metric.**

Here is what it does say about the online A/B test:

- **Test setup:** GenRec was tested on about 10% of Netflix traffic for 4 weeks, on key batch-compute surfaces (p. 6).
- **Overall result:** Under a low-data, low-signals configuration, GenRec showed "statistically significant improvement over the production baseline on both short-term and long-term online metrics" (p. 6).
- **Only number given:** There was a "+0.006% relative improvement on our core online metric," which the authors call "statistically meaningful at Netflix scale" (p. 6). The paper does not say whether this core metric is a short-term homepage engagement metric.
- **Figure 3:** This figure shows the online metrics for GenRec versus the production model (p. 6). Its values are not included in the text I have. Footnote 4, which is attached to the figure caption, is also not reproduced.

The document gives no p-values, confidence intervals, or metric-level breakdowns. Any such values may be in Figure 3 or its footnote, which I can't see.
